hypotheses.hypothesis: Per-quantity status management needs TWO separate fields: quantity_images for URLs, quantity_statuses for metadata.
hypotheses.lesson: CRITICAL ARCHITECTURE: Never mix data types in single field. quantity_images={qty: URL_string} for JavaScript compatibility. quantity_statuses={qty: {is_active, in_stock}} for management. Separate concerns = no conflicts.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Critical directories must be validated before deletion during cleanup operations.
hypotheses.lesson: CLEANUP SAFETY: sessions/ directory is REQUIRED by Django SESSION_FILE_PATH setting. Never delete directories without checking if they are referenced in settings.py or required by framework. Add .gitkeep to preserve empty critical directories in version control.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Comprehensive pre-launch audit is critical for production readiness and prevents security vulnerabilities.
hypotheses.lesson: PRODUCTION READINESS: Before deployment, systematically audit: 1) Security (DEBUG, SECRET_KEY, HTTPS, ALLOWED_HOSTS), 2) Functionality (all features tested), 3) Performance (optimized), 4) UX/UI (responsive), 5) Infrastructure (backup, monitoring). Create detailed documentation (audit report, deployment guide, quick checklist) and environment variable templates. This catches critical issues (like DEBUG=True in production) that could expose sensitive data.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Media library prevents file re-upload when accidentally selecting wrong file - users can browse and reselect from previously uploaded files.
hypotheses.lesson: UX ENHANCEMENT: When implementing file uploads, always provide a media library/gallery for re-selecting previously uploaded files. Users make mistakes and need ability to browse uploaded media without re-uploading. Implement: 1) API endpoint to scan media directory, 2) Modal gallery with grid layout, 3) Filters by category, 4) Search functionality, 5) Click-to-select with URL auto-fill. This saves time, reduces duplicate files, and improves user experience.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Modern CSS Variables are superior to SCSS for Django projects near production - no build step, instant updates, maintainable.
hypotheses.lesson: CSS ARCHITECTURE: For Django projects, use Modern CSS Variables instead of SCSS when: 1) Project near production (avoid new dependencies), 2) No complex calculations needed, 3) Want instant updates (no compilation). Benefits: NO build step, NO npm dependencies, simpler deployment, dynamic theming via JavaScript, better for small teams. Structure: variables.css (50+ custom properties), components.css (reusable classes), page-specific.css, main.css (imports all). Use @import, :root, var(), calc(). Result: 90% SCSS benefits, 0% complexity.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bright brand colors (like Monobank purple) are not suitable for admin panels used daily - cause eye strain.
hypotheses.lesson: UX/UI DESIGN: Admin panels need calm, comfortable color schemes for long work sessions. Avoid: 1) Bright brand colors (purple, pink), 2) Acid/neon colors, 3) High contrast gradients, 4) Strong glow effects. Use: 1) Darker backgrounds (#0f1419 vs #1a1d2e), 2) Muted accent colors (blue #3b82f6 vs purple #667eea), 3) Reduced opacity effects (0.15 vs 0.4), 4) Better text contrast. Result: comfortable for eyes, reduced fatigue, professional look, better readability. CSS Variables make theme changes instant across entire system.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Toast notifications are superior to Django's default messages display - better UX and don't disrupt content flow.
hypotheses.lesson: NOTIFICATIONS UX: Implement toast notifications instead of alert boxes or inline messages: 1) Non-intrusive (fixed top-right), 2) Auto-dismiss (5s), 3) Progress bar shows time, 4) Slide-in animation, 5) Multiple toasts stack, 6) Colored left border indicates type, 7) Close button for manual dismiss. Integrate with Django messages framework for seamless backend→frontend notifications. Provide JavaScript API (showSuccess, showError) for frontend actions. Result: professional UX, no content disruption, clear visual feedback, better than modal alerts.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Product type differentiation (main vs additional) is critical for accurate cart calculations and business logic.
hypotheses.lesson: CART CALCULATION: When adding products to cart, always include 'type' field to differentiate: 1) type: 'main' for primary products (flowers with quantity counts), 2) type: 'additional' for accessories/extras (not counted as flowers). This enables: accurate flower count for statistics, proper delivery cost calculation based on product value not accessory count, flexible business rules per product type. Separate itemsTotal (for delivery threshold) from cart.total (including delivery cost). Never assume all items in cart are the same type - explicit typing prevents calculation errors and enables future features like type-specific discounts or rules.

hypotheses.hypothesis: CSS pointer-events must be carefully managed when layering absolute positioned elements over interactive UI components.
hypotheses.lesson: POINTER-EVENTS MANAGEMENT: When using absolute positioned layers (like product image layers), ALWAYS set pointer-events: none on decorative/background layers to prevent blocking interactive elements. Problem: Product-image-container, product-layers, packaging-layer, flowers-layer, color-mask were blocking clicks on color-dot and quantity-btn buttons beneath them. Solution: 1) Add pointer-events: none to ALL decorative/background layers, 2) Add pointer-events: auto to ALL interactive elements (buttons, inputs, links), 3) Set proper z-index hierarchy (interactive elements z-index: 10+, background layers lower), 4) Test clickability on both desktop and mobile. Without this, users can't interact with UI even though buttons are visible and styled correctly. Critical for layered designs.

hypotheses.hypothesis: HTML disabled inputs don't send data in form POST - use readOnly for locked fields that must submit.
hypotheses.lesson: FORM INPUT ATTRIBUTES: NEVER use disabled for input fields that must submit their values in POST request. Disabled inputs are completely excluded from form data. Problem: hex_code.disabled = true when user selected transparent color → POST didn't include hex_code → backend validation error 'required fields missing'. Solution: Use readOnly instead. readOnly vs disabled: 1) readOnly: value submits in POST, user can't edit, can focus/select, included in form validation. 2) disabled: value NOT in POST, user can't interact, grayed out, excluded from validation. For auto-filled/locked fields that MUST submit (like transparent color): ALWAYS use readOnly + optional visual feedback (bg color). For fields that should NOT submit (like conditional inputs): use disabled. Critical distinction for forms with dynamic field states.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Progress bar milestones must be calculated based on items total EXCLUDING delivery cost, otherwise thresholds trigger incorrectly.
hypotheses.lesson: PROGRESS BAR CALCULATION: When implementing cart progress bars with reward milestones, ALWAYS separate items total from cart total. Problem: cart.total included delivery cost (e.g., 950 UAH items + 50 UAH delivery = 1000 UAH) → milestone at 1000 UAH triggered prematurely → user received reward without reaching actual threshold. Solution: 1) Create separate cart.itemsTotal property for items sum WITHOUT delivery. 2) Calculate delivery separately: deliveryCost = itemsTotal < threshold ? cost : 0. 3) cart.total = itemsTotal + deliveryCost (for display only). 4) Pass cart.itemsTotal to progress bar functions, NOT cart.total. 5) Milestone checks: cartTotal >= milestone.amount where cartTotal is items only. Rationale: Milestones should reflect spending on products, not service fees. User should spend 1000 UAH on items to get reward, not 950 UAH items + 50 UAH delivery. Critical for accurate marketing and customer satisfaction.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Gift rewards should be automatically added to cart when milestone achieved and displayed with special styling to differentiate from regular products.
hypotheses.lesson: GIFT AUTO-ADD SYSTEM: When implementing gift rewards in progress bars, automatically add them to cart for better UX. Implementation: 1) Create autoAddGiftToCart() function that triggers when rewards updated. 2) Check if gift already in cart (prevent duplicates) by checking item.isGift flag. 3) Search for gift in additional_products by title match to get correct image. 4) Add gift as cart item with: price=0, type='gift', isGift=true, original title (no emoji prefix). 5) Display gifts differently: green gradient background, '🎁 Подарунок: БЕЗКОШТОВНО' label instead of price, gift-item CSS class. 6) Allow removal from cart like regular items. Benefits: User sees instant gratification when reaching milestone, gift automatically included in order, clear visual differentiation, no price confusion. Critical: Match gift name exactly with product title for image lookup, use fallback image if not found, prevent duplicate additions with isGift flag check.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Cart counters must be recalculated from source data on every update, not rely on cached values, to prevent ghost items and incorrect counts.
hypotheses.lesson: CART COUNTER MANAGEMENT: When implementing cart systems with auto-add items (gifts, bonuses), ALWAYS recalculate counters from items array, never cache. Problem: After clearCart(), gift items remained visible, cart.count showed wrong number, order details not updated. Cause: cart.count was cached value not recalculated, updateCartDisplay() didn't recalculate count, gifts re-added by autoAddGiftToCart() before cart fully cleared. Solution: 1) updateCartCount() - ALWAYS recalculate: cart.count = items.reduce((sum, item) => sum + item.quantity, 0). 2) updateCartDisplay() - recalculate count AND update all detail fields (totalFlowerCount, totalItemsCount, totalOrderPrice). 3) clearCart() - reset ALL properties (items, total, count, itemsTotal, discount) then call all update functions (updateCartDisplay, updateCartCount, updateProgressBar). 4) Create removeGiftFromCart() to explicitly filter isGift items. 5) autoAddGiftToCart() - check if cart has non-gift items before adding, remove gifts if no reward or cart empty. 6) Export removeGiftFromCart() for cross-module access. Result: Counters always accurate, clear cart truly empties everything, no ghost items, order details always current. Critical for cart reliability.

aiInternalState.lastAnalysis: CART CLEAR BUG FIX: User reported critical bugs after clearing cart: 1) Gift item remained visible (ghost item), 2) Cart counters not updated (cart-count, total-items-count, total-order-price), 3) Order details section showed old values. Root causes: cart.count cached value not recalculated, updateCartDisplay() relied on cached count, autoAddGiftToCart() re-added gifts after clear, removeGiftFromCart() didn't exist. Solutions implemented: 1) CLEAR CART FIX: clearCart() now resets ALL properties (items=[], total=0, count=0, itemsTotal=0, discount=0), calls all update functions, explicitly calls removeGiftFromCart(). 2) COUNTER RECALCULATION: updateCartCount() and updateCartDisplay() now ALWAYS recalculate cart.count from items.reduce(). Never trust cached values. 3) GIFT REMOVAL: Created removeGiftFromCart() function that filters isGift items, exported to window.progressBarManager. autoAddGiftToCart() now checks if cart has non-gift items before adding, removes gifts if no reward. 4) ORDER DETAILS UPDATE: Added explicit recalculation and logging for totalFlowers, totalItemsCount, totalOrderPrice. 5) LOGGING: Added detailed console logs at each step of clear operation for debugging. Testing: After clear cart shows: items=[], count=0, total=0, cart icon shows 0, order details show 0, no ghost gifts. Result: Cart clearing now completely reliable, all counters accurate, no ghost items, proper gift lifecycle management (add when earned, remove when lost or cart cleared).
